children: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen floated plans to make Canada an associate member of the European Union, saying the bloc must urgently rethink its partnerships.

"I would like to work with you on opening the door for Canada to be the first associate member of the EU," von der Leyen told Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney during a speech in Strasbourg on Wednesday.
"We share one ocean, one set of values, one way of seeing the world. And we will now build our shared future as well," she said.

Her comments came as part of her annual State of the Union speech, in which she set out further plans to boost the bloc's economy, touching on a broad range of subjects from agriculture and climate to relations with China.
She said permits and financing can determine where investments are made and that the bloc needs to move much faster on permitting.
The EU needs a pact against gold-plating--where governments add extra restrictions or provisions on top of existing rules--if officials are serious about simplifying the region's regulations.

title: EU Chief Floats Plan to Make Canada First Associate Member
